suggestion: Filter based on the actual Fundable List section designation in the source document rather than a hardcoded rank number, or verify and document that rank <= 11 exactly matches the fundable range for this specific document.

issue: The disadvantaged logic checks 'estimated_post_user_rate > mhi * .01' using raw dollar values, but the dictionary specifies the condition as 'Estimated Post-Project User Rate (per 4,000 gallons) exceeds one percent of MHI' — MHI is an annual figure, so dividing by 12 may be needed to compare monthly rate to monthly income, or the comparison should be annual. The current comparison multiplies annual MHI by 0.01, which is not the same as 1% of monthly MHI.
suggestion: Clarify whether MHI in the source is annual or monthly. If annual, the condition should likely be 'estimated_post_user_rate > (mhi / 12) * 0.01' to compare monthly rate against 1% of monthly MHI, or adjust accordingly per state definition.

No' which becomes 'pwsid_no' as well. Confirm both map to 'pwsid_no' identically after clean_names; a mismatch would cause the pwsid column to be all NA for one file.

issue: The post-processing special case checks: pwsid == 'IN5245047, IN, IN5245067'. However, the PWSID splitting logic prepends 'IN' to each token, so a value like '5245047, , 5245067' (with an empty token from a double comma or trailing comma) would produce 'IN5245047, IN, IN5245067'. This means the special case may only trigger if there is genuinely an empty token in the source. This is fragile — if the source data for Cedar Lake changes formatting slightly, the match will silently fail and the malformed PWSID will persist.
suggestion: Add a step to filter out empty/whitespace tokens after splitting PWSID, before prepending 'IN'. This prevents spurious 'IN' tokens. Also consider using grepl instead of exact equality for the Cedar Lake correction to be more robust.

issue: The Q1 MHI values are formatted as '$39,943.00' (with dollar sign, commas, and decimal) while Q4 MHI values are formatted as '$49,855' (with dollar sign and commas, no decimal). The convert_to_numeric function must handle both formats. If it strips only '$' and ',' but not '.00', numeric conversion should still work. However, if any MHI value is 'TBD' or blank (Q4 has 0% NA but values could still be non-numeric strings), convert_to_numeric must return NA, and then the disadvantaged case_when will evaluate NA < 43460 as NA (not FALSE), potentially defaulting to 'No' incorrectly or causing unexpected NA results. The MHI value $40,333 for Andrews appears in both files and is below $43,460, so it should be 'Yes' — verify this is correctly classified.
suggestion: Ensure convert_to_numeric handles both decimal and non-decimal dollar formats. Add explicit NA handling in the disadvantaged case_when: treat NA mhi or NA estimated_post_user_rate as unknown rather than defaulting to 'No'. Consider adding a case for NA values to return 'No Information'.

issue: Several Q4 rows have 'TBD' in the Estimated Post-Project User Rate column (e.g., Jackson County Water Utility row 2 shows 'TBD'). convert_to_numeric(..., TRUE) presumably returns NA for 'TBD'. When estimated_post_user_rate is NA, the conditions 'estimated_post_user_rate > 45' and 'estimated_post_user_rate > mhi * .01' both evaluate to NA, not FALSE. In case_when, NA conditions are skipped, so if mhi is also >= 43460 and rate is TBD, the project falls through to 'No' — but the true disadvantaged status cannot be determined. This could produce incorrect 'No' classifications.
suggestion: Add an explicit case before the TRUE ~ 'No' fallback: when is.na(estimated_post_user_rate) and mhi >= 43460, return 'No Information' to flag uncertain disadvantaged status.

issue: The logic uses requested_funds == '' to detect missing values and fall back to estimated_total_project_cost. However, in the Q4 data, the Requested Funds column has 3.1% NA (not empty string). read.csv() typically reads missing cells as NA, not ''. The condition requested_funds == '' will be FALSE for NA values (NA == '' returns NA in R), so the .default branch will be taken, passing NA to clean_numeric_string. This means the estimated_total_project_cost fallback is never triggered for the one Q4 row in the 'APPLICATIONS ONLY' section that needs it.
suggestion: Change the condition to: is.na(requested_funds) | requested_funds == '' to correctly handle both NA and empty string cases.

suggestion: str_squish is applied in both files which should handle leading/trailing spaces. However, consider also normalizing to a canonical form (e.g., removing all internal spaces or replacing with a separator) to guard against inconsistent spacing in the source CSVs.
